$comment: The CLI⇄GUI parity matrix (#645, brief §3). One row per basic CLI command or flag. 'gui' lists the data-control ids of the GUI controls that do the same thing; each control id belongs to exactly one row. A basic row must have every gui control rendered on some route, or be 'pending' on its slice issue (684-689). Every rendered control must appear in a row or in 'chrome'. Each row's command and flags must exist in the generated CLI reference (docs/gen/<cli>/<command>.md, synced from the shipped binaries). Checked by parity/matrix.ts: statically in gates/matrix-static.test.ts, against the rendered app in e2e/matrix.spec.ts.

rows.note: GPU sizes lead here or to a watch, never to a plain launch (owner decision D6 on #645)

chrome.$comment: Controls that are the app itself, not a CLI command. Each needs a reason. Adding a control here instead of a row needs the same review as a new CLI command.
chrome.chrome.skip-link: Skip to content: navigation within the page.
chrome.chrome.menu: Opens the navigation on narrow screens.
chrome.chrome.nav-help: Help pages: documentation, not a command.
chrome.chrome.account-menu: Shows which account and location you are in.
chrome.chrome.settings: Opens Settings, the portal's own preferences.
chrome.chrome.settings-advanced: The basic/advanced level is a GUI preference with no CLI equivalent (D3).
chrome.chrome.sign-in: Sign-in. The CLI equivalent is `aws login`, not a spore.host command (slice 1, #684).
chrome.chrome.sign-out: Sign-out drops the in-memory credentials; nothing on AWS changes.
chrome.chrome.reauth: Sign in again before credentials expire.
chrome.chrome.details: Opens 'Details for support' on an error.
chrome.chrome.dialog-cancel: The safe choice in a confirm dialog; does nothing.
chrome.chrome.issue-link: Links a stub page to its tracking issue. Gone once the slice ships.
chrome.chrome.footer-link: Site footer: home, documentation, privacy, terms.
